title: 4-Digit by 1-Digit Multiplication Word Problems
intro: Use an area model to explain multiplication with a four-digit factor.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Split the long side into thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones. Label and add the partial areas before introducing the shorter written method.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Length: 4,307 feet. Width: 6 feet.

4,307 × 6 = 25,842

The area is 25,842 square feet.

Ask your student

Why does this partial product have a different place value?

If your student needs help

If a zero is missing, compare the written product with the value of its rectangle section.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set contains four rectangle-area stories. Lengths range from 1,000 to 9,999 feet, and widths range from one to nine feet. A width of one is allowed: multiplying by one leaves the numerical value unchanged, while the answer still names square feet. Zero-width rectangles and missing-side questions are not included.
